title: Opportunistic slot reshaper with KV smoothing and SLO fallback policies
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Problem: Continuous batching provides excellent throughput but is vulnerable to tail-latency spikes when KV working sets and GPU memory pressure vary across tenants. Existing preemptors are aggressive and treat all interrupts as equal, which causes oscillation for mid-priority tenants and unnecessary KV thrashing. Goal: Implement a slot reshaper that opportunistically reconfigures active slice allocations based on short-term KV residency forecasts and a smoothing policy; combine this with a layered SLO fallback policy that prefers graceful degradation (reduced batch depth / soft cap) over hard preemption and full KV eviction when possible.
design_notes:
- Introduce a lightweight 'slot reshaper' that runs on each inference worker every 50ms and computes a proposed delta to per-tenant slots based on: recent completion rates, KV hit ratio trend, and estimated post-sequence KV retention.
- KV smoothing: when the reshaper reduces a tenant's slot allocation, mark a 'soft hold' on frequently-accessed KV pages for 500-2000ms to avoid immediate eviction. Soft hold uses a tiny aging credit so long-lived hot KV entries avoid churn.
- SLO fallback layers: 1) soft-cap batch depth reduction (lowest impact on throughput); 2) redirect to lower-memory model variant or quantized variant; 3) targeted KV partial eviction using LRU within a tenant slab; 4) full tenant preempt (last resort).
- Decision signals: per-request latency percentile drift, GPU free memory delta, KV cache pressure (slots to resident ratio), tenant priority weight, and time-since-last-eviction.
- Telemetry: expose per-reshaper decision traces, a histogram of soft-hold durations, and per-tenant fallback counts to Console for alerting and RCA.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Spike): build an in-process mock reshaper that consumes existing metrics and emits a plan; run in simulated mode against production traces to validate oscillation reduction.
Phase 2: implement real-time reshaper on worker with atomic slot adjust APIs guarded by a token. Implement KV soft-hold markers in cache metadata and a compact aging credit.
Phase 3: integrate SLO fallback controller with routing for model variant and batch depth adjustment. Add unit and e2e tests under the 'batching-runtime' test harness.
Phase 4: gradual rollout (canary on Dedicated pools, 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with metrics-driven rollback criteria (no more than 1.5x increase in P95 latency for high-priority tenants, KV churn decrease >= 20%).
acceptance_criteria:
- Reshaper runs at <=50ms CPU overhead per worker under 90% load.
- KV churn (measured as unique eviction count per minute per worker) reduced by >=20% under mixed workloads compared to baseline.
- For a mixed-tenancy 95th percentile latency-sensitive test, fewer than 5% of preempt events should be full tenant preempts; majority should be soft-cap or variant fallback.
- Console shows new dashboards: reshaper decisions, soft-hold histogram, per-tenant fallback breakdown.
- Feature toggles to disable soft-hold or switch SLO fallback order without restart.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: soft-hold increases memory residency and may push some workers over OOM. Mitigation: soft-hold is token-limited per worker and will be preemptible by a global OOM signal.
- Risk: reshaper oscillates allocations across tenants. Mitigation: apply exponential backoff and a minimum hold window (250ms) for resized slots.
- Risk: wrong model-variant redirects reduce quality. Mitigation: attach a prompt-aware quality score threshold and per-tenant opt-out flag.
- Risk: telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample 1% of decisions in high-traffic pools and aggregate counters otherwise.
timeline: 2026-03-01: Spike start; 2026-03-08: Spike results and design review; 2026-03-12: Begin Phase 2 implementation; 2026-03-22: Phase 2 internal testing; 2026-03-26: Canary rollout; 2026-03-28: Full rollout target (subject to canary metrics)
